title: a16z Podcast: The Dream of AI Is Alive in Go

reader_summary.source_label: From the episode notes — transcript not yet available
reader_summary.headline: Why are people so fired up about a computer winning yet another game?
reader_summary.overview: Why are people so fired up about a computer winning yet another game? Whether it's checkers, chess, Jeopardy, or the ancient Chinese game of Go, we get excited about the potential for more when we see computers beat humans. But then nothing "big" -- in terms of generalized artificial intelligence -- seems to happen after that burst of excitement.

key_points.text: it's like the dream of the 1990s (and 1980s, and 1970s, and 1960s) is alive in Seoul right now.
a16z's head of research and deal team Frank Chen and board partner Steven Sinofsky -- who both suffered through the last “AI winter” -- share how everything old is new again.
